title: Direct Exposure of Domain Entities over Remote APIs
damaged_code:
```rust
#[derive(Serialize)]
struct UserEntity {
    id: u64,
    username: String,
    password_hash: String, // Secret leaked!
    created_at: DateTime<Utc>,
}
```
pattern: Returning core domain aggregates or database entities directly through remote public endpoints (like REST or gRPC).
why_bad: It creates a brittle contract. Any refactoring of the internal domain representation or database schema instantly breaks the public API contract, and risks leaking sensitive internal fields.
detection: Look for structs annotated with both database-mapping macros (e.g., `#[derive(Queryable)]`) and serialization macros (e.g., `#[derive(Serialize)]`) that are returned directly by controller functions.
counterexample: Trivial CRUD applications with no business logic where entities match the API payload exactly. Marked `Context-dependent`.
fix: Decouple the API contract by introducing a distinct Data Transfer Object (DTO) and a mapping layer.
source: *Implementing Domain-Driven Design* by Vaughn Vernon (2013), p. 512, 675.
